title: Checks for uses of the assert keyword.
summary: Assertions are removed when Python is run with optimization requested (i.e., when the -O flag is present), which is a common practice in production environments. As such, assertions should not be used for runtime validation of user input or to enforce interface constraints. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.116.

title: Checks for uses of the builtin exec function.
summary: The exec() function is insecure as it allows for arbitrary code execution. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.116.

title: Checks for files with overly permissive permissions.
summary: Overly permissive file permissions may allow unintended access and arbitrary code execution. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.211.
message_templates: `os.chmod` setting a permissive mask `{mask:#o}` on file or directory
`os.chmod` setting an invalid mask on file or directory

title: Checks for hardcoded bindings to all network interfaces (0.0.0.0).
summary: Binding to all network interfaces is insecure as it allows access from unintended interfaces, which may be poorly secured or unauthorized. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.116.

title: Checks for potential uses of hardcoded passwords in strings.
summary: Including a hardcoded password in source code is a security risk, as an attacker could discover the password and use it to gain unauthorized access. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.116.

title: Checks for potential uses of hardcoded passwords in function calls.
summary: Including a hardcoded password in source code is a security risk, as an attacker could discover the password and use it to gain unauthorized access. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.116.
message_templates: Possible hardcoded password assigned to argument: "{}"

title: Checks for potential uses of hardcoded passwords in function argument defaults.
summary: Including a hardcoded password in source code is a security risk, as an attacker could discover the password and use it to gain unauthorized access. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.116.
message_templates: Possible hardcoded password assigned to function default: "{}"

title: Checks for the use of hardcoded temporary file or directory paths.
summary: The use of hardcoded paths for temporary files can be insecure. If an attacker discovers the location of a hardcoded path, they can replace the contents of the file or directory with a malicious payload. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.211.
message_templates: Probable insecure usage of temporary file or directory: "{}"

title: Checks for uses of the try-except-pass pattern.
summary: The try-except-pass pattern suppresses all exceptions. Suppressing exceptions may hide errors that could otherwise reveal unexpected behavior, security vulnerabilities, or malicious activity. Instead, consider logging the exception. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.237.

title: Checks for uses of the try-except-continue pattern.
summary: The try-except-continue pattern suppresses all exceptions. Suppressing exceptions may hide errors that could otherwise reveal unexpected behavior, security vulnerabilities, or malicious activity. Instead, consider logging the exception. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.245.

title: Checks for uses of the Python requests or httpx module that omit the timeout parameter.
summary: The timeout parameter is used to set the maximum time to wait for a response from the server. By omitting the timeout parameter, the program may hang indefinitely while awaiting a response. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.213.
message_templates: Probable use of `{}` call without timeout
Probable use of `{}` call with timeout set to `None`
